# Exponent-4 Bruck section for the fixed order-96 envelope

**Reproduction and fixed-pair uniqueness, with scoped independent review below.** Let $`G`$ be the 40-point group generated by Nagy's permutations in [arXiv:0709.4544v1](https://arxiv.org/html/0709.4544v1), Lemma 3.2, and let $`H=N_G(P)`$ for the indicated Sylow 5-subgroup. Put $`J=O_2(G)`$, $`M=[G,J]`$, and let $`z`$ be the unique nonidentity element of $`J\cap H`$. The proposed result is that


```math
K_4=M\cup zc^G,
```


where $`c`$ is any involution outside $`J`$, is the **unique faithful Baer section of a simple exponent-4 Bruck loop for this fixed pair $`(G,H)`$**. It defines a simple proper Bruck loop of order 96. This neither classifies all order-96 loops nor excludes other groups or stabilizers. It continues [C0010](../../claims/0010.md), with no new permanent claim ID.

The [standalone verifier](../code/verify_bruck96_exponent4.py) independently constructs this section, checks the folder and identities, and exhausts the normal subgroup lattice. The argument and certificate have the two scoped independent reviews recorded below.

## Determining the section

Nagy, loc. cit. Lemmas 3.3–3.4, gives $`|G|=3840`$, $`|J|=32`$, $`|M|=16`$, $`G/J\cong S_5`$, and the unique nonradical involution class $`c^G`$ of size 80. The module $`J`$ is the six-point permutation module modulo its constant line. The verifier independently checks its action against the concrete 40-point group and finds $`\dim\mathop{\mathrm{Hom}}\nolimits_{S_5}(J^*,J)=1`$, by solving all intertwining equations for the two six-point generators.

For an exponent-4 Bruck section, the [elementary inversion reduction](bruck-s5-elementary-inversion.md), accepted by an independent check at exact source the recorded source revision under its stated inputs, identifies its nonzero inversion derivation with a nonzero map $`J^*\to J`$. It is therefore unique. In the concrete group, conjugation by $`z`$ gives that nonzero derivation: $`z`$ centralizes $`H`$ and $`J`$, but not $`G`$. Thus the section's canonical inversion is $`\tau=\mathop{\mathrm{conj}}\nolimits(z)`$.

The marked set $`zK`$ is $`G`$-conjugacy-invariant and consists of involutions. By Baumeister–Stein [arXiv:0908.2597v1](https://arxiv.org/html/0908.2597v1), Lemmas 4.1–4.2 and 4.5, $`D=K\cap J`$ has size 16 and the remaining elements lie over the ten transpositions. The radical part $`zD`$ is a conjugacy-invariant subset of $`J`$, contains $`z`$, and has size 16. The verifier obtains the four $`G`$-orbit sizes $`1,6,10,15`$; the orbit of $`z`$ has size 6. The only union of these orbits of size 16 containing $`z`$ is $`J\setminus M`$, so $`D=M`$. The outer part of $`zK`$ is nonempty and lies in the unique nonradical involution class, hence is $`c^G`$. This forces $`K=K_4`$.

## Source comparison and verification

Baumeister–Stein, [*Self-invariant 1-Factorizations of Complete Graphs and Finite Bol Loops of Exponent 2*](https://www.math.uni-bielefeld.de/~baumeist/BS.pdf), author preprint dated 8 December 2008, Remark 3.5, p. 9, reports a MAGMA-checked exponent-4 Bruck section in the same group and stabilizer as its Aschbacher loop. In that notation $`z=v_1`$, and their representative $`v_1y_*n_*`$ belongs to the unique nonradical involution class; hence $`y_*n_*=zc`$. Their radical part is $`M`$, and their outer part is $`(zc)^{JH}`$. The verifier checks in the concrete Nagy model that


```math
(zc)^{JH}=zc^G,
```


both sets having 80 elements. Identification of the published source's fixed pair with this Nagy pair uses the source's Theorem 3, p. 3: its order-96 insoluble exponent-2 loop is unique up to isomorphism in that size range, and a loop isomorphism induces an isomorphism of Baer envelopes. The published theorem reports computer calculations; this comparison does not claim an independently constructed permutation-by-permutation isomorphism between the two source models.

Run from the repository root, with assertions enabled:

```sh
python3 problems/0323-finite-simple-non-moufang-bol-loops/code/verify_bruck96_exponent4.py
```

The script is standalone, uses only the Python standard library, and writes no files. With Python 3.12.14 in this workspace, its run took 1.93 seconds wall time. It checks $`|G|=3840`$, $`|H|=40`$, $`|J|=32`$, $`|M|=16`$, core-freeness, generation by $`K_4`$, the six-point module identification and Hom dimension, all relevant conjugacy orbits, and the source-style orbit identity. It checks transversality to every conjugate of $`H`$, inverse and twisted-subgroup closure, the left Bol identity and AIP. The element-order distribution is $`1^1,2^{15},4^{80}`$; the deterministic non-Moufang witness has table indices $`(1,0,28)`$, with index 0 the identity. The verifier constructs the left-coset loop; taking the opposite transports it to the right-sided source convention.

For a separate simplicity check the script enumerates all normal subgroups by joining normal closures of all conjugacy classes. It finds orders $`1,16,32,1920,3840`$. The proper nontrivial subgroups of orders 16 and 32 have section-image sizes 21 and 11, respectively, while $`[G:HR]=6`$ in each case; the other nontrivial normals satisfy $`HR=G`$. The normal-subloop criterion in [C0001, Theorem 2.2](../foundations/C0001.md), applied via opposite transport, therefore gives simplicity. These are finite computational checks plus the cited criterion, not a claim of formal verification or of a new unrestricted classification.

## Independent review

Independent checks an independent check and an independent check independently accepted the fixed-pair argument and standalone verifier at exact source the recorded source revision, conditional on the cited inversion and normal-subloop results. Both independently ran the certificate with Python 3.12.14 and accepted its group, module, folder, identity, order-distribution and normal-subgroup checks. The source comparison was checked against the cited Nagy and Baumeister–Stein statements; it retains its dependence on the source-reported exponent-two uniqueness theorem. The reviews establish the stated fixed-pair result, not an unrestricted order-96 census or formal verification.
